title: Stream abort contract and backfill playbook for hosted SSE partial outputs
creator: Marisol Chen
description:
Summary: Multiple customers across Hosted and Dedicated tiers reported truncated or duplicated partial streaming responses when network interruptions occur mid-request. In several private deployments we saw proxies/doorkeepers terminate connections during backend model expansion, leaving clients with unusable partial outputs. This ticket defines a server-side abort contract, deterministic backfill strategy, and a safe rollout for a hotfix that heals partial outputs without surprising duplicate tokens or violating client-side idempotency expectations.

Impact: Customer-facing applications (chat UIs, longer document generation) observed: 1) partial final tokens that cannot be safely resumed by clients, 2) duplicate token tails when the client retries, and 3) clients that treated a truncated SSE as an error and retried leading to 2x cost and bad UX. High-severity escalations were opened by two enterprise customers and one platform partner.

Root cause analysis (summary):
- We currently accept connection termination as a hard stop and do not emit an explicit "abort" sentinel in the event stream.
- Our resume protocol relies on opaque session checkpoints which are not always flushed to durable metadata on connection tear-down, particularly when edge LB/proxy resets occur during request bootstrapping.
- When clients resend the request, the serving layer can re-generate overlapping suffix tokens (non-idempotent across restarts) because the KV cache and kernel scheduling state may diverge under preemption.
- Private deployments with aggressive TCP timeouts or proxy rewriting caused the server to believe the session had fully finished, skipping backfill attempts.

Goals for this ticket:
1) Define and implement a minimal abort contract emitted to SSE clients so client libraries can distinguish "clean finish", "server abort with resume token", and "unrecoverable abort".
2) Add a best-effort backfill path that, given a known resume token, will produce a deterministic suffix for the client to merge (or ignore) without duplicating tokens.
3) Ensure the fix is safe for Dedicated/Private (customer-managed infra) where metadata durability assumptions are weaker.
4) Ship a hotfix + conservative rollout and an expanded observability surface to detect regressions.

Acceptance criteria:
- Server emits a final control event before closing SSE when possible: {type: "final", code: "OK" | "ABORT_RESUMABLE" | "ABORT_UNRECOVERABLE", resume_token: <opaque>} (contract documented).
- If ABORT_RESUMABLE + resume_token issued, a subsequent client resend with the token will produce a deterministic, token-aligned suffix that the client SDK can merge without duplication.
- In cases where resume_token cannot be issued (edge reset before checkpoint flush), server emits ABORT_UNRECOVERABLE; client SDKs should fall back to application-level retry.
- New metrics and alerts: abort-rate-by-model, abort-resumable-ratio, backfill-success-rate, post-backfill-token-duplications.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Durability model: We will persist minimal resume metadata to a fast, strongly-consistent store (etcd-backed per-host journal) synchronously at a cheap checkpoint boundary (first output token and then periodic KV cache anchors). This increases tail latency slightly for long sessions but dramatically reduces unrecoverable aborts.
- Determinism: Backfill will prefer reading from persisted KV anchors and, when available, will re-run the last N decoder steps under a deterministic scheduler to reconstruct suffix tokens. For quantized/optimized runtimes where exact determinism is impossible, we will instead emit a conflict-safe delta: a short idempotent sentinel + final-state hash and a patch operation clients can apply.
- Client SDK behavior: SDKs will be updated to recognize the control event and perform merge logic rather than blind concatenation. For older SDKs we will add a compatibility header that instructs server to include a "safe-merge" wrapper around resumed output to prevent duplicates.

Implementation plan:
1) Server: Add abort control event emission and resume_token generation; implement persist-on-checkpoint to local per-pod store (ENG).
2) Backfill engine: deterministic re-play for supported runtimes; conflict-safe deltas for unsupported runtimes (ENG + Research).
3) Client SDKs: v4.1 patch to handle control events and merge heuristics; compatibility mode for v<4.1 (SDK).
4) Ops: telemetry, dashboard, and alerting changes (Console + Observability).
5) Private/Dedicated docs: rolling upgrade guidance and optional compatibility flag for environments that cannot adopt the persist-on-checkpoint model immediately.

Rollout plan:
- Canary (1%): runtime-1.22 with models parked under "sse-canary" in hosted. Observe abort-resumable-ratio and backfill-success-rate for 72h.
- Gradual ramp: 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% over two weeks if no regression.
- Dedicated/Private: epoxy: deliver runtime bits and an ops-runbook for partners to enable safe checkpointing. Default remains off for private until partner enables persist-on-checkpoint or opts into compatibility wrapper.

Monitoring & Runbooks:
- Add alert: abort-resumable-ratio > 5% for 30m triggers P1; post-backfill-token-duplications > 0.05% triggers immediate rollback and investigation.
- Update restart/runbook: "SSE late-abort investigation", with steps to gather session logs, resume_token snapshots, and backfill trial replays.

Customer communication:
- Drafted email templates for affected customers describing the abort contract, expected client SDK update, and suggested mitigation (temporary client-side merge heuristics) while we roll the fix.
- Marisol to lead escalations sync and set up 1:1 with two enterprise customers on 2025-11-24.

Next steps (short-term):
- Spike: implement minimal control-event emission and a no-op resume_token to prove client-visible contract (2 days, Lukas + Asha).
- Engineering PR for persist-on-checkpoint design doc (due 2025-11-27).
- Create canary config and dashboards (obs eng) before 2025-11-30.

Longer-term:
- Evaluate extending deterministic replay to quantized runtimes (research project).
- Postmortem and root-cause documentation for the three escalations with timelines and communications.

Links: Attachments and artifacts are below in the attachments field.

Notes: This ticket spans runtime, client SDKs, and ops — requires cross-functional coordination. If we cannot reach an agreed persistence model for Private within two weeks, we will ship the compatibility wrapper as mandatory for Hosted and optional for Private.
